newsitem.title: USA: Key West-Cuba parasailing trip planned.
newsitem.headline: Key West-Cuba parasailing trip planned.

text.p: The son of a former Key West mayor plans to parasail across the Straits of Florida to Cuba on the anniversary of his father's famous water-skiing jaunt to Havana 19 years ago.
Sean McCoy, whose father Sonny McCoy skied the 90 miles (144 km) from Key West to Havana on Sept. 10, 1978 at age 50, will make the trip beneath a brightly colored parasail flying a large U.S. flag.
"I think it would be a lot of fun. I'd have a little something in common with my dad," McCoy said.
The crossing will take at least four hours and McCoy might reach an altitude of 1,000 feet (300 metres).
The pilot of the tow boat, Key West parasailing entrepreneur Mark diSabatino, said he hoped the flight would win an entry in the Guinness Book of Records for longest and highest parasail ride.

A Cuban sponsor will cover the cost of an overnight stay at Cuba's Varadero tourist area east of Havana in order to keep the crew from running afoul of the U.S. embargo, which prevents spending by U.S. tourists, diSabatino said.
DiSabatino said there is no political message in the trip and admitted it was more publicity stunt than athletic achievement.
